lines.english: He turned his thoughts to something else,
Wealthy Jakyp entrusted to Oshpur
The boy who bore the name Chong Jindi.
Chyiyrdy wept and cried aloud,
Putting her belt around her neck,
Pleading, calling out to Oshpur Bai:
‘My dear Oshpur Bai,
You were a giant lying in the valley,
You were in charge of wealthy Jakyp’s many sheep.
We have abundant wealth, but no children;
This child we had when we were all but dead—
lines.note: The phrase literally says ‘seen when dead,’ apparently emphasizing how late or desperately the child was obtained.

lines.english: There is no way to curb his wildness.
I have made a silk coat; have him wear it,
Among the horses is Toruchaar;
Catch that splendid steed and have him ride it,
Be sure to fasten the Kalmyk stone to the crown of his head.
lines.note: The identity and purpose of the ‘Kalmyk stone’ are unclear.

lines.english: I have placed him in your hands as a sacred trust;
Care for him for another four years!’
Once Oshpur had taken the boy,
Once wealthy Jakyp had stayed behind there,
He put him on Toruchaar,
Clothed him in the ashes of silk,
lines.note: ‘The ashes of silk’ is the literal reading of ‘торконун күлүн’; the intended fabric or expression is uncertain.

lines.english: And, taking his chances, toward the sheep
Brave Oshpur led him away.
When Manas went to Oshpur,
He had not yet become Manas,
Your hero had not yet come to bear the name Manas.
